reconcile.connective: Henry resolves the count by noting that describing one of two men isn't false, only partial — Mark never claims there was only one.

discrepancy.connective: Steve Wells presses the plain-reading count: Matthew says two men met Jesus while Mark and Luke each describe only one, a straightforward numerical clash.

skeptic.name: Steve Wells
skeptic.work: The Skeptic's Annotated Bible, "How many men were possessed with devils?" (skepticsannotatedbible.com/contra/possessed.html)
skeptic.attribution: Steve Wells, The Skeptic's Annotated Bible, "How many men were possessed with devils?"

excerpts.excerpt_text: In Matthew, they were said to be two possessed with devils; here it is said to be a man possessed with an unclean spirit. If there were two, there was one, and Mark doth not say that there was but one; so that this difference cannot give us any just offence; it is probable that one of them was much more remarkable than the other, and said what was said.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: States the numeric divergence explicitly (two in Matthew vs. one here) and gives the standard harmonization: naming one of two is not the same as denying a second, so Mark's singular is compatible with Matthew's plural.

pd_work.resource: John Haley, An Examination of the Alleged Discrepancies of the Bible (1874), p. 387
pd_work.author: John Haley
pd_work.note: Haley lists this exact pair in his 'different numbers' table — 'Demoniacs, Luke viii. 27 and Matt. viii. 28 (only the more prominent one mentioned by Luke)' — grouping it with the two-blind-men case as a class of Gospel divergences resolved by one writer naming only the more notable member of a pair.
